 In The Court Of The Metropolitan Magistrate
 Traffic Court - Iv, Bangalore

 Metropolitan Magistrate
 Traffic Court - Iv, Bangalore
 Dated : This The 27th Day Of March 2024 
 C.C. No.2843/2020 
Complainant: State by Hulimavu Traffic Police
 Station, Bangalore
 (Represented by: APP)
 V/S.
ACCUSED: 1) Muttuswamy S., S/o. Subbaiah,
 Age: 49 years,
 R/at No.205, 2nd cross,
 2nd main road,
 Near Food World,
 Gottigere, Bannerghatta road,
 Bangalore - 83  (Represented by: Sri Manju M.)
1. Date of commission of offence : 13082019 2. Offences alleged against accused : U/s.279 & 304(A) of IPC,
Sec.66 R/w.192(A) of  M.V.Act 3. Date of recording of evidence : 18022022 4. Date of closing evidence : 02122023 5. Date of judgment : 27032024  ***
 2  C.C.No.2843/2020  JUDGEMENT The Police Inspector of Hulimavu Traffic Police Station has filed the charge sheet against the accused for the offences punishable U/s.279 and 304(A) of IPC, Sec.66 R/w.192(A) of M.V.Act.
2. The brief case of the prosecution is that:
On 13082019 at about 21.10 p.m. within the jurisdiction of Hullimavu Traffic police station, the accused being the driver of Bolero Jeep vehicle bearing registration Hulimavu Trps vs Muthuswamy S on 27 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111166666/
1 No.KA51/A8730 drove the same on Bannerghatta main road, near Chaitanya hotel, from kalenaagrahara towards Gottigere, suddenly took a right turn without any intimation in rash a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and dashed to Motor cycle vehicle bearing registration No.KL274458 which was proceeding in opposite direction the said road. Due to the impact the rider Arun Babu, aged 24 years sustained grievous head injuries and the pillion rider sustained simple injuries. Later the rider succumbed to death. Further the accused vehicle was not possessing a valid permit on the day of accident. Thereby the accused is alleged to have committed the offences punishable U/s.279 and 304(A) of IPC, Sec.66 R/w.192(A) of M.V.Act.
C.C.No.2843/2020 3. Upon taking cognizance, case came to be registered against accused for the offences punishable U/s.279 & 304(A) of IPC, Sec.66 R/w.192(a) of M.V.Act. The accused appeared before the court through his counsel & got enlarged on bail. Charge sheet copies furnished to the accused and thereby provision U/s..207 of Cr.P.C. duly complied with. 
4. Plea came to be framed for the offences U/s.279 & 304(A) of IPC, Sec.66 R/w.192(A) of M.V.Act,
for which accused pleaded not guilty claimed to be tried.
5. During the course of trial, the prosecution has examined P.W.1 to 4 and got exhibited documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.4. On completion of prosecution side evidence, the statement of accused U/s.313 of Cr.P.C. was recorded and the accused denied all the incriminating evidence appearing against him and did not choose to lead any defence evidence. 
6. Heard arguments on both sides. 
7. The points that arise for my consideration are as follows:
1.Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on 13082019 at about 21.10 p.m. within the jurisdiction of Hullimavu Traffic police station, the accused being the driver of Bolero Jeep vehicle bearing C.C.No.2843/2020 registration No.KA51/A8730 drove the same on Bannerghatta main road, near Chaitanya hotel, from kalenaagrahara towards Gottigere in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life, thereby the accused has committed an offence punishable U/s.279 of IPC?
2. Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on the above said date, time and place the accused being the driver of the said vehicle, drove his vehicle in the above said manner he dashed to Motor cycle vehicle bearing registration No.KL27 4458 which was proceeding in opposite direction the said road. Due to the impact the rider Arun Babu, aged 24 years sustained grievous head injuries and the pillion rider sustained simple injuries. Later the rider succumbed to Hulimavu Trps vs Muthuswamy S on 27 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111166666/
2 death, thereby the accused has committed an offence punishable U/s.304(A) of IPC? 
3. Whether the prosecution further proves that the accused vehicle was not in possession of permit of the vehicle on the day of accident, thereby the accused has committed an offence punishable U/s.66 R/w. Sec.192(a) of M.V.Act? 
4. What order? 
8. My answer to the above points are as under:
POINT No.1: IN THE NEGATIVE POINT No.2: IN THE NEGATIVE POINT No.3: IN THE AFFIRMATIVE POINT No.4: AS PER THE FINAL ORDER For the following C.C.No.2843/2020 REASONS 9. POINT No.1 and 2: For the sake of convenience and to avoid repetition of facts, these points are taken up for common discussion to have brevity.
10. It is the case of the prosecution that on 13082019 at about 21.10 p.m. within the jurisdiction of Hullimavu Traffic police station, the accused being the driver of Bolero Jeep vehicle bearing registration No.KA 51/A8730 drove the same on Bannerghatta main road, near Chaitanya hotel,
from kalenaagrahara towards Gottigere, suddenly took a right turn without any intimation in rash a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and dashed to Motor cycle vehicle bearing registration No.KL274458 which was proceeding in opposite direction the said road. Due to the impact the rider Arun Babu, aged 24 years sustained grievous head injuries and the pillion rider sustained simple injuries. Later the rider succumbed to death. Further the accused vehicle was not possessing a valid permit on the day of accident. Thereby the accused is alleged to have committed the offences punishable U/s.279 and 304(A) of IPC, Sec.66 R/w.192(a) of M.V.Act.
C.C.No.2843/2020 11. In order to prove its case the prosecution examined 4 witnesses as P.W.1 to P.W.4 and marked 4 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.4.
12. C.W.3/ Tejas Mathew is examined as P.W.1 who is the eye witness of this case. He deposed that on 13082019 at about 9.10 p.m. after finishing his work he was proceeding from Kalena Agrahara towards Gottigere, near Chaitanya hotel one two wheeler bearing registration No.KL274458 coming from opposite side from Gottigere, at that time one Bolero vehicle bearing registration No.KA51A8730 turned towards right side at that time accident has taken place. Due to the impact Ajithbabu and Arun babu sustained injuries and he shifted them to Vijayashree hospital in an auto. In this regard he has given statement before police. The accident has taken place due to Bolero suddenly turned right side. He has identified the accused present before the court. On 17 082019 police conducted spot mahazar and obtained his signature. On 29082019 police called him to police station and informed that the injured Arun Babu is dead. In this regard he has given further statement. 
Hulimavu Trps vs Muthuswamy S on 27 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111166666/
3 During his crossexamination by accused counsel he deposed that currently he is working in Tamil Nadu C.C.No.2843/2020 and at the time of accident he was studying in T.John College. He does not know the C.W.2 i.e., another eye witness and mahazar witness. At the time of accident he was proceeding to his home after completing his work. He further deposed he was doing part time job in Dominos at that time and he was proceeding in his bike behind the Bolero vehicle. The width of the road was 30 mtrs. He admits that there is a road hump prior to accident spot and there is a bus stand near the road hump. He admits the injured was also studying in T.John college. He does not know in which college deceased was studying. He deposed that he does not know whether rider and pillion rider are the students of T.John college. He admits it is a busy road. He admits there is a police station at a distance of 100 mtrs from the accident spot and deposed the rider sustained injuries on his right leg. He denied the suggestions of the accused counsel. 
13. C.W.13/ Venkateshaiah H.B. is examined as P.W.2 who is the 2 nd Investigation Officer of this case. On 29082019 he received the case file from C.W.12 and conducted further investigation. He received the information from the hospital about the death of the injured in this case. On account of receipt of death memo, he sent requisition to court for inclusion of C.C.No.2843/2020 Sec.304(A) of IPC. On the same day he visited Victoria hospital he conducted inquest mahazar between 11.00 to 1.00 p.m in the presence of C.W.4 to 7 and body was sent to postmortem. He received the postmortem report On the same day he visited accident spot. When the case file was checked, it was found that the accused vehicle was not having permit on the day of accident. After completion of investigation he has filed a Charge Sheet against the accused. During his crossexamination by the accused counsel he denied the suggestions of the accused counsel. 
14. C.W.10/ Thippeswamy is examined as P.W.3 who is IMV inspector. He deposed that on 1708 2019 he received requisition from Hulimavu traffic police station and he conducted the inspection of light motor vehicle bearing registration No.KA51A8730 and another motor vehicle bearing registration No.KL274458. In his report he has stated that the right front bumper and front right side mudguard of light motor vehicle got damaged and two wheeler's front right crush guard and the mirror got damaged. He has stated that the break system of the vehicle was in order and in his opinion the accident was not caused due to the mechanical defect of the vehicle and gave the report. 
C.C.No.2843/2020 During his crossexamination by the accused counsel he deposed that generally they identify the vehicle on the basis of engine number and chassis number. He admits he has not seen the chassis number of the examined vehicle. He admits he has not mentioned about fresh damages in his report and denied the suggestions of the accused counsel. 
15. C.W.09 / Dr. Pradeep is examined as P.W.4 who is Doctor. He deposed that on 29082019 he received requisition from Hulimavu traffic police station to examine a male body aged about 24 years. After receiving the requisition he has conducted postmortem over the dead body between 2.00 to 2.45 p.m. and prepared his report and given the same to the investigating officer. 
During his crossexamination by the accused counsel he deposed that he has not mentioned the timings of the death and deposed that if a person fell from any building there is a chances of such injuries. He denied the suggestions of the accused counsel. 
Hulimavu Trps vs Muthuswamy S on 27 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111166666/
4 16. Out of the documents marked for prosecution Ex.P.1 is the spot mahazar, Ex.P.2 is the Inquest mahazar, Ex.P.3 is the P.M. Report and Ex.P.4 is the IMV Report. 
C.C.No.2843/2020 17 . In the instant case the prosecution is alleging that the accused being the driver of Bolero drove his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner in middle of the public road and all of a sudden taken a right turn and dashed to two wheeler, due to his negligent act accident has taken place and one person succumbed to death and prosecution contended that accused committed the offences punishable U/s.279 & 304(A) of IPC. Section 279 IPC deals with rash and negligent driving of any vehicle or riding on a public way in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life or likely to cause hurt or injury to any person. In order to constitute an offence U/s.279 of IPC, it must be established that the accused was driving the vehicle on a public way in rash and negligent manner to endanger human life or to likely cause to hurt or injury to any other person. For the purpose of section 279 rash and negligent may be described as criminal rashness or criminal negligence. It must be more than mere carelessness of error of judgment. The essential ingredients of section 279 are: (1) rash and negligent driving or riding on a public way, (ii) The act must be such as to endanger human life or likely to cause hurt or injury to any person. In the instant case accused being the driver of the vehicle parked his vehicle in a negligent C.C.No.2843/2020 manner and since he has not taken precautionary measures to intimate the other persons moving in the road by putting reflectors and indicator lights due to his negligent act the deceased drove his vehicle and dashed to accused vehicle later untoward incident has taken place, prosecution has contended that due to the negligent act of the accused the accident has taken place hence it comes within the purview of Sec.279 of IPC. The bare perusal of the provision and intent of the makers of act makes it clear all negligent act which result in further acts will attract section. 279 of IPC.
18. In order to constitute offence U/s.304(a) of IPC the prosecution must establish the essential ingredients of Sec.304(A) of IPC which are as follows: (I) The death of the person must be in question (ii) The death must have caused by the accused; and (iii) The act of the accused was rash or negligent and it did not amount to culpable homicide. 
19. In the case on hand the prosecution is alleging that accused being the driver of the four wheeler drove his car in rash and negligent manner and caused the accident due to which the deceased succumbed to death. The prosecution has to establish that accused drove his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner in order C.C.No.2843/2020 to fix the liability U/s.279 and 304(a) of IPC. Now "rashness" for the purpose of above said sections, has been understood to mean a hasty act done without considering the possible result. The criminality lies in running the risk of doing an act with indifference to consequences. Criminal negligence on the other hand is the gross and culpable neglect to take proper care and precaution to guard against injury either to the public generally or to an individual in particular, which having regard to all the circumstances out of which the charge has arisen, it was the imperative duty of the accused person to have adopted. Essentially, criminal negligence is the breach of duty towards others. 
Hulimavu Trps vs Muthuswamy S on 27 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111166666/
5 20. It is a settled preposition of law that rash and negligent behavior has to be examined in light of the facts and circumstances of a given case. The two are incapable of being construed or seen in isolation and must be examined in light of the attending circumstances. 
21. To prove their case, the prosecution has examined four witness among them, one is eye witness and one is investigating officer, motor vehicle inspector and the doctor who conducted the postmortem. In the instant case the prosecution did not examine the C.C.No.2843/2020 complainant and independent eye witness. The complaint is marked by the prosecution the investigating officer who registered the complaint and started investigation is not examined by the prosecution as he is suffering from serious illness and not in a position to appear before the court. 
The complainant and eye witnesses were not secured by the prosecution, hence court after giving sufficient opportunity and after issuing proclamation in view of their non sccurrence they were dropped. 
22. The prosecution as based his case on P.W.1 who is claimed as eye witness of this case. The said witness deposed in chief examination that the accused has not taken any precautionary measure before taking right turn and due to which accident has taken place. He did not speak anything about the negligent act of the accused and did not mention anything about the rashness on the part of the accused. The said witness in his crossexamination at one point he deposes he was a student in St.John college and at another point he deposed that he was doing part time job in Dominos. But he did not mention the timings of his part time job. On the alleged day according to witness he was proceeding home after conclusion of his work. Admittedly the accident has taken place at around 9.00 p.m. in a busy C.C.No.2843/2020 road. The same witness admits it is a one way road and density of traffic is relatively high. The witness deposed that the accused all of a sudden take a right turn and dashed to two wheeler which was proceeding in the opposite lane. In the accident the rider sustained injuries and later succumbed to death. The P.W.1 was proceeding behind the Bolero and he cannot say what has happen in front of the Bolero, what he can say is the thing which he see after the accident. The accident has taken place in night hours and as per the admission of the witness there is no street light facility which means accident has taken place during night. When there is no lighting arrangement the signal given in the front is not visible to the person proceeding from back side. The only allegation is accused taken a sudden right turn due to which collusion taken place. As discussed earlier the witness cannot say about signals given by the accused driver since he cannot see the same. Moreover he has not speaken about rashness or negligence of the accused. He himself admits the deceased were not wearing the helmet and he cannot say the speed of the two wheeler at the time of the accident. The best witness who can depose about the accident is the pillion rider. The pillion rider is complainant according the charge sheet, what injuries was sustained by the pillion rider is not mentioned in the C.C.No.2843/2020 charge sheet and his wound certificate is also not produced before the court, the prosecution did not secure his presence before the court which raises question about the genuineness of the case of the prosecution. 
23. The other examined witnesses are the investigating officer who conducted inquest mahazar,
collected postmortem report and motor vehicle inspection report and later submitted final report before the court. He is not the investigating officer who recorded the statement of the witness or visited the spot and conducted mahazar at accident spot. Since he has not recorded the statements Hulimavu Trps vs Muthuswamy S on 27 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111166666/
6 and visited accident spot, he can depose only about his duty and his evidence is of no use to prosecution to prove the rash and negligent act unless corroborated by other evidence. The prosecution further examined the motor vehicle inspector and the doctor who conducted postmortem. They deposed about their certificates and they cannot say anything about the rashness or negligence on the part of the accused. 
24. Upon analyzing the statement of the witnesses and documents submitted by both sides, in the instant case it is the contention of the accused that he is not responsible for the accident and accident has taken place due to the negligence of the two wheeler rider who C.C.No.2843/2020 drove the vehicle in high speed and negligent manner. He contend that he has not caused any death as stated by prosecution. Their contention is the accident occurred due to negligence of the deceased and police are blaming the same on the innocent accused. In the instant case Rash and negligent act of the accused auto driver is the vital point to book him U/s.279 IPC or section 304(A) IPC. There is no any dispute regarding the accidental death of the deceased person as it was not denied by the defence. 
25. The witnesses have not stated rash and negligent act on the part of the accused on the date of alleged incident. Further eye witnesses have not stated the rash and negligent act of the accused to show his involvement. The prosecution has not examined the material witnesses i.e., the complainant and independent eye witness, the examined eye witness appears to be the student of the college where the deceased and complainant was studying and as per his version he cannot say what has happen in front of the vehicle without such things the element of rashness and negligence cannot be established. Therefore, in this circumstance of the case, the case of prosecution regarding rash and negligent act and also regarding C.C.No.2843/2020 involvement of the vehicle of accused could not be made out beyond reasonable doubt. 
26. Therefore, looking to the evidence available on record and the materials placed by way of oral and exhibits, the case of prosecution appears to be doubtful. There is doubt as to whether the accused drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger the human life and personal safety of others. Therefore, in the circumstances of the case, as per the rules of criminal justice if any doubt arise about the commission of the act then such doubt shall be in favour of accused. The prosecution has failed to prove the alleged offence against the accused. Accordingly,
the points under consideration are answered point No.1 and 2 IN THE NEGATIVE. 
27. POINT No.3: It is further alleged that the prosecution that the accused was driving the Bolero does not have permit to ply on the said route on the alleged day of accident. The witness was informed about the said aspect and he has not produced any valid documents to substantiate his claim that on alleged day the vehicle was having permit. The accused did not choose to lead defence evidence and not produced documentary evidence before the court and no question was asked to C.C.No.2843/2020 investigating officer with regard to this aspect and no document is confronted to the witness. The prosecution has discharged its burden it is for the accused to rebutt the same but he has not done that. Hence point No.3 answered in affirmative. 
Hulimavu Trps vs Muthuswamy S on 27 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111166666/
7 28. POINT No.4: In view of the above discussions and findings I proceed to pass the following ORDER Acting U/sec. 255(1) of Criminal procedure code, the accused is hereby acquitted of the offences alleged against him punishable U/sec. 279 and 304(A) of IPC.
Acting under Sec.255(2) of Criminal Procedure Code, the accused is hereby convicted of the offence alleged against him punishable U/Sec.66 R/w 192 of IMV Act. 
Accused is hereby directed to pay fine of Rs.2,000/ for the offences punishable U/s.66 R/w.192 of IMV Act. in default shall undergo SI for 3 months. 
Bail bonds of accused and surety bonds shall stand canceled after completion of appeal period. 
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer, typed by her, corrected and then pronounced by me in the open Court this the 27 th day of March 2024). 
(GAGAN M.R.) MMTC - IV, BANGALORE.

Pradeep 2. LIST OF DOCUMENTS MARKED FOR THE PROSECUTION:
Ex.P.1: Spot mahazar Ex.P.2: Inquest mahazar Ex.P.3: P.M. report Ex.P.4: IMV Report 3. LIST OF WITNESSES EXAMINED FOR THE ACCUSED:
NIL 4. LIST OF DOCUMENTS MARKED FOR THE ACCUSED:
NIL (GAGAN M.R.) MMTC - IV, BANGALORE.

In the instant case the prosecution is alleging that the accused being the driver of Bolero drove his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner in middle of the public road and all of a sudden taken a right turn and dashed to two wheeler, due to his negligent act accident has taken place and one person succumbed to death and prosecution contended that accused committed the offences punishable U/s.279 & 304(A) of IPC. Section 279 IPC deals with rash and negligent driving of any vehicle or riding on a public way in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life or likely to cause hurt or injury to any person.

In order to constitute an offence U/s.279 of IPC, it must be established that the accused was driving the vehicle on a public way in rash and negligent manner to endanger human life or to likely cause to hurt or injury to any other person.
For the purpose of section 279 rash and negligent may be described as criminal rashness or criminal negligence.
It must be more than mere carelessness of error of judgment.

The essential ingredients of section 279 are: (1) rash and negligent driving or riding on a public way, (ii) The act must be such as to endanger human life or likely to cause hurt or injury to any person.

In the instant case accused being the driver of the vehicle parked his vehicle in a negligent C.C.No.2843/2020 manner and since he has not taken precautionary measures to intimate the other persons moving in the road by putting reflectors and indicator lights due to his negligent act the deceased drove his vehicle and dashed to accused vehicle later untoward incident has taken place, prosecution has contended that due to the negligent act of the accused the accident has taken place hence it comes within the purview of Sec.279 of IPC.

The bare perusal of the provision and intent of the makers of act makes it clear all negligent act which result in further acts will attract section. 279 of IPC.

In order to constitute offence U/s.304(a) of IPC the prosecution must establish the essential ingredients of Sec.304(A) of IPC which are as follows: (I) The death of the person must be in question (ii) The death must have caused by the accused; and (iii) The act of the accused was rash or negligent and it did not amount to culpable homicide.

19. In the case on hand the prosecution is alleging that accused being the driver of the four wheeler drove his car in rash and negligent manner and caused the accident due to which the deceased succumbed to death.
The prosecution has to establish that accused drove his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner in order C.C.No.2843/2020 to fix the liability U/s.279 and 304(a) of IPC.
Now "rashness" for the purpose of above said sections, has been understood to mean a hasty act done without considering the possible result.
The criminality lies in running the risk of doing an act with indifference to consequences.

Criminal negligence on the other hand is the gross and culpable neglect to take proper care and precaution to guard against injury either to the public generally or to an individual in particular, which having regard to all the circumstances out of which the charge has arisen, it was the imperative duty of the accused person to have adopted.
Essentially, criminal negligence is the breach of duty towards others.

21. To prove their case, the prosecution has examined four witness among them, one is eye witness and one is investigating officer, motor vehicle inspector and the doctor who conducted the postmortem.
In the instant case the prosecution did not examine the C.C.No.2843/2020 complainant and independent eye witness.

The complaint is marked by the prosecution the investigating officer who registered the complaint and started investigation is not examined by the prosecution as he is suffering from serious illness and not in a position to appear before the court.

The complainant and eye witnesses were not secured by the prosecution, hence court after giving sufficient opportunity and after issuing proclamation in view of their non sccurrence they were dropped.
22. The prosecution as based his case on P.W.1 who is claimed as eye witness of this case.
The said witness deposed in chief examination that the accused has not taken any precautionary measure before taking right turn and due to which accident has taken place.
He did not speak anything about the negligent act of the accused and did not mention anything about the rashness on the part of the accused.
The said witness in his crossexamination at one point he deposes he was a student in St.John college and at another point he deposed that he was doing part time job in Dominos.
But he did not mention the timings of his part time job.
On the alleged day according to witness he was proceeding home after conclusion of his work.
Admittedly the accident has taken place at around 9.00 p.m. in a busy C.C.No.2843/2020 road.
The same witness admits it is a one way road and density of traffic is relatively high.
The witness deposed that the accused all of a sudden take a right turn and dashed to two wheeler which was proceeding in the opposite lane.
In the accident the rider sustained injuries and later succumbed to death.
The P.W.1 was proceeding behind the Bolero and he cannot say what has happen in front of the Bolero, what he can say is the thing which he see after the accident.
The accident has taken place in night hours and as per the admission of the witness there is no street light facility which means accident has taken place during night.
When there is no lighting arrangement the signal given in the front is not visible to the person proceeding from back side.
The only allegation is accused taken a sudden right turn due to which collusion taken place.
As discussed earlier the witness cannot say about signals given by the accused driver since he cannot see the same.
Moreover he has not speaken about rashness or negligence of the accused.
He himself admits the deceased were not wearing the helmet and he cannot say the speed of the two wheeler at the time of the accident.
The best witness who can depose about the accident is the pillion rider.

The pillion rider is complainant according the charge sheet, what injuries was sustained by the pillion rider is not mentioned in the C.C.No.2843/2020 charge sheet and his wound certificate is also not produced before the court, the prosecution did not secure his presence before the court which raises question about the genuineness of the case of the prosecution.

23. The other examined witnesses are the investigating officer who conducted inquest mahazar,
collected postmortem report and motor vehicle inspection report and later submitted final report before the court.
He is not the investigating officer who recorded the statement of the witness or visited the spot and conducted mahazar at accident spot.

Since he has not recorded the statements Hulimavu Trps vs Muthuswamy S on 27 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111166666/
6 and visited accident spot, he can depose only about his duty and his evidence is of no use to prosecution to prove the rash and negligent act unless corroborated by other evidence.
The prosecution further examined the motor vehicle inspector and the doctor who conducted postmortem.
They deposed about their certificates and they cannot say anything about the rashness or negligence on the part of the accused.

24. Upon analyzing the statement of the witnesses and documents submitted by both sides, in the instant case it is the contention of the accused that he is not responsible for the accident and accident has taken place due to the negligence of the two wheeler rider who C.C.No.2843/2020 drove the vehicle in high speed and negligent manner.
He contend that he has not caused any death as stated by prosecution.
Their contention is the accident occurred due to negligence of the deceased and police are blaming the same on the innocent accused.
In the instant case Rash and negligent act of the accused auto driver is the vital point to book him U/s.279 IPC or section 304(A) IPC.
There is no any dispute regarding the accidental death of the deceased person as it was not denied by the defence.
25. The witnesses have not stated rash and negligent act on the part of the accused on the date of alleged incident.
Further eye witnesses have not stated the rash and negligent act of the accused to show his involvement.

The prosecution has not examined the material witnesses i.e., the complainant and independent eye witness, the examined eye witness appears to be the student of the college where the deceased and complainant was studying and as per his version he cannot say what has happen in front of the vehicle without such things the element of rashness and negligence cannot be established.

Therefore, in this circumstance of the case, the case of prosecution regarding rash and negligent act and also regarding C.C.No.2843/2020 involvement of the vehicle of accused could not be made out beyond reasonable doubt.
26. Therefore, looking to the evidence available on record and the materials placed by way of oral and exhibits, the case of prosecution appears to be doubtful.
There is doubt as to whether the accused drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger the human life and personal safety of others.
Therefore, in the circumstances of the case, as per the rules of criminal justice if any doubt arise about the commission of the act then such doubt shall be in favour of accused.
The prosecution has failed to prove the alleged offence against the accused.

Accordingly,
the points under consideration are answered point No.1 and 2 IN THE NEGATIVE.
27. POINT No.3:
It is further alleged that the prosecution that the accused was driving the Bolero does not have permit to ply on the said route on the alleged day of accident.
The witness was informed about the said aspect and he has not produced any valid documents to substantiate his claim that on alleged day the vehicle was having permit.

The accused did not choose to lead defence evidence and not produced documentary evidence before the court and no question was asked to C.C.No.2843/2020 investigating officer with regard to this aspect and no document is confronted to the witness.
The prosecution has discharged its burden it is for the accused to rebutt the same but he has not done that.
Hence point No.3 answered in affirmative.
